areas.name: Bangkok from above
areas.thai: กรุงเทพฯ จากเบื้องบน
areas.description: All of Bangkok at once. Every building in the OpenStreetMap coverage rendered as a 3D extrusion in BKKx signal yellow, faded low so the Esri satellite still reads. The whole-city view uses opacity 0.32 — the silhouette of a working city, not a solid block.

areas.name: Rattanakosin
areas.thai: รัตนโกสินทร์
areas.description: The 18th-century walled city on the east bank of the Chao Phraya. Grand Palace, Wat Pho, Wat Phra Kaew, the National Museum, the old defensive canals.

areas.name: Yaowarat (Chinatown)
areas.description: Bangkok's commercial heart for two centuries. Gold shops by day, street food by night. Soi Texas, Talat Mai, the temple Wat Traimit with the solid-gold Buddha.

areas.name: Sukhumvit
areas.description: Bangkok's longest road as a single coherent district. Nana, Asok, Phrom Phong, Thonglor, Ekkamai, On Nut — a stacked gradient of foreign embassies, malls, expat housing, and night markets.

areas.name: Silom / Sathorn
areas.thai: สีลม / สาทร
areas.description: Tower cluster on the east of the old city. Stock Exchange of Thailand, the original skyscrapers, Lumphini Park, Patpong night market, the Indian textile quarter on Pahurat just to the west.

areas.name: Chatuchak
areas.description: The 35-acre weekend market, the largest in Southeast Asia. Surrounded by the Chatuchak Park, Queen Sirikit Park, the train market (Talat Rot Fai), and a dense network of sois.

areas.name: Khao San
areas.description: Five blocks of guesthouses, bars, tattoo shops and pad thai. The starting point for overland travelers since the 1980s. Anchors the north end of Rattanakosin to Banglamphu.

areas.name: Phaya Thai
areas.chapter: Where the BTS meets the airport
areas.description: The two rail systems cross: BTS Sukhumvit and the Airport Rail Link. Surrounding it are the Baiyoke Tower II, Pratunam wholesale market, the old government hospital belt.

areas.name: Victory Monument
areas.thai: อนุสาวรีย์ชัยสมรภูมิ
areas.description: Bangkok's busiest roundabout — and a 50 m bayonet monument that the building layer used to miss entirely (OSM tags it historic, not building). Buses, vans, the BTS viaduct, and the old airport expressway all meet here.

areas.name: Ari
areas.description: A leafy sois off Phahonyothin Road: cafes, design shops, weekend brunch, the old Rama VI bridge approach. A working-class neighborhood that gentrified without losing its grid.

areas.name: Thonglor / Ekkamai
areas.thai: ทองหล่อ / เอกมัย
areas.description: Two BTS stops that became Bangkok's most concentrated strip of bars, restaurants, and condos. Japanese expat, fashion shoots, late-night izakaya, design hotels.

areas.name: Chao Phraya Riverside
areas.thai: แม่น้ำเจ้าพระยา
areas.description: The 372-km Chao Phraya running through the city. Riverside temples (Wat Arun on the Thonburi bank, Wat Kalayanamit, Santa Cruz), the IconSiam mall, the Oriental, the river boats.

areas.name: Lumphini Park
areas.thai: สวนลุมพินี
areas.description: Bangkok's first public park (1920s), shaped by the same landscape architect as Manhattan's Central Park. Monitor lizards, paddle boats, surrounded by the densest tower cluster in the city.

areas.name: Chulalongkorn University
areas.thai: จุฬาลงกรณ์มหาวิทยาลัย
areas.description: Thailand's oldest university (1917), a self-contained 600-rai campus in the middle of the city. Green quads, the Centenary Park, the CU Sports Complex, surrounded by the Pathumwan and Siam commercial belts.

areas.name: Don Mueang
areas.description: Bangkok's original airport (1914), now low-cost carrier hub. The Royal Thai Air Force Museum, the old terminal, and the eastern approach of the BTS extension.

areas.name: Ratchathewi
areas.description: The rail lines, markets and superblocks that pull Bangkok toward Victory Monument, Pratunam and Makkasan. A district defined by what passes through it.
